split.cv: 5-fold KFold on the training split, shuffled, seed 42

excluded_features.Price_Premium: It is the ticket price minus the base fare, which puts the answer inside a feature.
excluded_features.Base_Price_At_Booking: It is the ticket price minus the premium, so it also comes from the target.
excluded_features.Seats_Sold_Realized: It is the final number of seats sold for the departure, which is not known when a fare is quoted.
excluded_features.Remaining_Seats_Realized: It is total seats minus final seats sold, which is not known when a fare is quoted.
excluded_features.Load_Factor: It is final seats sold over total seats, which is not known when a fare is quoted.

data_notes: The data is synthetic. In it, fares rise with booking lead time for about three weeks and then level off (mean £48.70 same day, about £77 from 15 days out). That is the opposite of real UK advance fares. The model reproduces the data and is not pricing advice.
Bookings are front-loaded. A third are same-day and only 655 of 519,713 are more than 60 days out, so the curve beyond 60 days rests on thin data.
Demand_Index is one score per departure in the source data. The demo treats it as the operator's demand forecast, available when quoting.
